findings.title: Shared-level and leaderboard traffic uses unauthenticated HTTP
findings.code_excerpt:
public final static String USERLEVELS_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoClock4k/get_level.php";
	public final static String HIGHSCORE_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoClock4k/get_highscore.php";
findings.entry_point: Traffic to the four HTTP endpoints declared in ApoClockConstants.java:5-9 becomes attacker-controlled when the apo-games.de server is malicious or an attacker controls DNS/routing on the victim's network.
findings.sink: Raw URLConnection streams send and receive level data at ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.java:121-140 and 162-204, and score data at ApoClockHighscoreLoad.java:81-103 and 125-155.
findings.data_path: Startup reaches ApoClockPanel.init() at ApoClockPanel.java:95-98, then loadUserlevels() at lines 139-146, ApoClockUserlevels.loadUserlevels() at ApoClockUserlevels.java:22-32, and ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.load(). Entering Arcade starts ApoClockHighscore.loadHighscore() through ApoClockArcarde.java:37-45. Editor uploads follow ApoClockEditor.java:166-183 to ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.save(); score submissions follow ApoClockArcarde.java:84-89 to ApoClockHighscoreLoad.save().
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker on the victim's Wi-Fi intercepts the initial cleartext request. They can replace downloaded leaderboard entries, modify an outgoing score, or return a crafted shared-level record. The last option reaches the game parser described in ApoClock-02 and can hang the victim's game.
findings.preconditions: The device reports an active network at ApoClock.java:36-48, the Android build permits cleartext HTTP, and the attacker controls the server or the network path.
findings.validation_plan: Run the app or an emulator through an HTTP interception proxy. Launch the app and enter Arcade to observe plaintext requests for get_level.php and get_highscore.php; complete/upload a level and finish an Arcade game to observe the plaintext POSTs. Rewrite one response or POST parameter and confirm that the client consumes or sends the modified value without any TLS or authenticity failure.

findings.title: Downloaded level can set a zero clock interval and hang the update loop
findings.entry_point: The first line of every 11-line record returned by get_level.php is accepted as an untrusted level string at ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.java:179-204.
findings.sink: The parsed velocity is stored without validation by ApoClockEntityClock.java:17-20. ApoClockPuzzleGame.think() uses it as the threshold at line 226 and subtracts it at line 238; a value of zero makes the while loop permanently true without changing curTime.
findings.data_path: ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.load() adds the response line at ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.java:182-184; ApoClockUserlevels.getAllLevelsSorted() copies it at ApoClockUserlevels.java:44-54; Puzzle's userlevels button calls setPuzzleGame() at ApoClockPuzzle.java:63-66; ApoClockPanel.java:234-248 calls ApoClockPuzzleGame.loadLevel(); and ApoClockPuzzleGame.java:134-153 parses the five fields into an ApoClockEntityClock.
findings.attack_scenario: A malicious server or HTTP interceptor supplies a syntactically complete record whose level line is "240,260,40,0,0" and whose remaining ten metadata lines contain valid numbers/text. The victim opens Puzzle, selects userlevels, and taps to start. The next update enters the loop at ApoClockPuzzleGame.java:226 and never exits, producing an ANR or requiring the game to be killed.
findings.preconditions: The crafted record must be downloaded successfully, the victim must select the shared level and tap to start it, and cleartext level traffic must be permitted. A malicious uploader can use the same route if save_level.php stores arbitrary submitted level strings; the client upload contains only the URL-encoded level at ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.java:121-133, but server-side validation was not available to verify.
findings.validation_plan: Use an HTTP proxy to answer get_level.php with eleven lines: level "240,260,40,0,0", then valid values such as time 1, count 1, total 1, name x, four zero ratings, id 1, and current time 0. Launch the app, enter Puzzle > userlevels, select the level, and tap outside the navigation controls. Capture a thread dump or ANR trace showing the update thread repeating ApoClockPuzzleGame.java:226-238.

findings.title: Automatic level download consumes an unbounded response
findings.entry_point: A malicious get_level.php server or HTTP interceptor controls the entire response read from the URLConnection opened at ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.java:162-179.
findings.sink: The loop at ApoClockUserlevelsLoad.java:182-207 has no byte, line-length, record-count, or time bound and retains response fields in multiple ArrayLists. Afterward, ApoClockUserlevels.sortByUpload() performs a nested insertion sort at ApoClockUserlevels.java:57-74.
findings.data_path: ApoClockPanel.init() automatically invokes loadUserlevels() at ApoClockPanel.java:95-98; its thread calls ApoClockUserlevels.loadUserlevels() at ApoClockPanel.java:139-146 and ApoClockUserlevels.java:22-28; load() then reads until attacker-controlled EOF. The same unbounded read pattern is repeated for user-triggered leaderboard loading at ApoClockHighscoreLoad.java:142-158 and is collapsed into this finding.
findings.attack_scenario: On every launch, an interceptor returns a very large number of valid 11-line records or one extremely long first line. readLine() and the lists grow until memory is exhausted; if the response eventually ends, the quadratic sort can consume prolonged CPU. The app may be killed for memory pressure or remain busy without ever making shared levels available.
findings.preconditions: The app must see an active network and initiate the automatic level request; the platform must permit the HTTP connection; the attacker must control its response.
findings.validation_plan: Proxy get_level.php and generate increasingly large but syntactically valid 11-line records with equal numeric values. Launch the app while recording heap use and the loader thread. Confirmation is unbounded heap growth, an OutOfMemoryError/process kill, or sustained execution in ApoClockUserlevels.java:57-74 after EOF. Separately, withhold EOF or newlines to confirm there is no read timeout.

findings.title: Online leaderboard accepts scores asserted entirely by the client
findings.entry_point: The player-controlled client supplies name, points, and clock count. Arcade computes points only in local mutable state at ApoClockArcardeGame.java:219-237, while the name is taken from the local text field at ApoClockArcarde.java:84-89.
findings.sink: ApoClockHighscoreLoad.save() writes the three values directly to save_highscore.php at lines 81-100 with no session identifier, gameplay proof, nonce, signature, or authenticator in the request body at lines 92-96.
findings.data_path: A completed Arcade game calls ApoClockPanel.setAracardeHelp() at ApoClockArcardeGame.java:250-267; ApoClockPanel.java:253-263 invokes ApoClockArcarde.setPoints(); ApoClockArcarde.java:84-89 calls ApoClockHighscore.saveHighscore(); its thread at ApoClockHighscore.java:64-75 reaches ApoClockHighscoreLoad.save().
findings.attack_scenario: A cheating player intercepts their own score POST or instruments the app, replaces points with a much larger integer, and forwards the request. Because the request carries only client assertions, the server has no submitted evidence from which to reconstruct the run. If save_highscore.php stores such requests, the attacker obtains a forged shared leaderboard position.
findings.preconditions: The endpoint must be reachable and persist client submissions. Server-side range or rate checks could limit particular values, but no server implementation was supplied; independent verification of the claimed run is impossible from the three submitted fields alone.
findings.validation_plan: Against an authorized staging or cloned endpoint, complete any qualifying Arcade run through an HTTP proxy and change the points field before forwarding. Then request get_highscore.php and confirm the modified value appears. Repeat with a direct form POST to determine whether the endpoint requires any state not present in the client request.

findings.title: Unlocked progression is trusted directly from local preferences
findings.entry_point: The local ApoClockPref SharedPreferences file opened with mode 0 at ApoClock.java:39 supplies the solved integer when the app starts.
findings.sink: ApoClockPanel passes the value to solvedLevel() at ApoClockPanel.java:119-126 and 349-351. ApoClockPuzzleChooser.setSolved() trusts it and marks levels available at ApoClockPuzzleChooser.java:65-76; touch handling permits every index up to that value at lines 81-86.
findings.data_path: A local user edits the solved entry in the app-private preference XML; ApoClockPanel.loadPreferences() reads it at lines 118-126; solvedLevel() calls ApoClockPuzzleChooser.setSolved(); and the chooser uses the resulting field as its only progression gate.
findings.attack_scenario: On a rooted or debuggable device, a player stops the app, changes the solved preference to 29, and restarts it. Level 30 becomes selectable without completing the preceding levels. The gain is confined to cheating progression on that installation and does not itself forge the online leaderboard.
findings.preconditions: The user needs root, run-as/debug access, a permitted backup/restore path, or another means to modify the app-private SharedPreferences file. An ordinary sandboxed application cannot edit another app's mode-0 preferences.
findings.validation_plan: On a rooted or authorized debuggable emulator, stop net.apogames.apoclock, edit shared_prefs/ApoClockPref.xml so solved is 29, restart, and open the puzzle chooser. Confirm that the last built-in level is selectable before any earlier level is completed.

notes: Review scope was all 28 ApoClock src Java files, both generated Java files, and four security-relevant bundled dependency files. Local persistence uses SharedPreferences at ApoClock.java:39 and ApoClockPanel.java:118-136; no .cheat, .mar, .skunk, .defence, or .rep parser appears. Source-wide searches found no ObjectInputStream, MessageDigest, custom ClassLoader/defineClass, user.home, user.dir, or Applet entry point. The bundled AndModPlug PlayerThread can pass caller-supplied bytes into JNI at PlayerThread.java:234-240 and loads the fixed name modplug-1.0 at PlayerThread.java:74 and 910-913. However, no ApoClock source imports or calls that package, and the provided adapter reads packaged Android resources at MODResourcePlayer.java:91-124; no attacker-controlled native path was therefore established, so this was not reported as unsafe_native_call. The separate decompiled MIDI library likewise has no ApoClock callsite.
